comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1 complete) — confirmed root cause, with the discriminating experiments

### The mechanism, in two parts

**(1) The budget now sits inside the band of legitimate test costs.** Commit `6a5c88027c5`
(story `bold-abeyant-indri`) lowered the per-test hang budget 300 s -> 20 s at
`pyproject.toml:650`, `_build-and-test.yml:662` and `:677`. `git blame -w -C -M` on all three
lines returns `6a5c88027c59` and nothing else; its trailer is `rebar-ticket: 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce`.

The direct PARENT commit `4d6c1cc835e` — same day, same runner class, same
`-n 4 --dist worksteal --cov=rebar`, still on `--timeout=300` — passed clean
(run 32581500417 / job 97051623657: `16182 passed, 66 skipped in 906.38s`, zero crashes) and
its own `--durations=25` block reports fourteen tests between **18.71 s and 29.93 s of `call`
time**, headed by 29.93 s / 28.72 s / 22.97 s / 22.63 s / 22.46 s / 22.44 s / 21.63 s. That list
IS the crash list. So the evidence refuting "20 s is measured, not guessed: the default tier
runs clean at it" was already in CI at the moment the change landed. `timeout_func_only = true`
cannot rescue it: those are `call` times — the test body is the whole-tree scan.

The story's own measurement ("the whole unit tier runs clean at `--timeout=20`, 5097 passed") was
a LOCAL unit-tier run — no `--cov=rebar`, no `tests/scripts`, faster cores. The gating
`ubuntu-latest, py3.13` leg is the only one that adds coverage, and it is the only leg that reds.

**(2) `timeout_method = "thread"` expresses an expiry as a process kill, not as a verdict.**
`pytest_timeout.py:542` (`timeout_timer`) calls `os._exit(1)` from the watchdog thread, so the
xdist worker dies outright. Only the `signal` method reports `Failed: Timeout`, via
`pytest.fail()` at `pytest_timeout.py:502`. **A budget expiry inside an xdist worker can
therefore NEVER print `Failed: Timeout`** — it prints `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`
followed by `worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<test>'`.

This resolves the tension the report flagged: the zero `Failed: Timeout` count is a *prediction*
of the mechanism, not evidence against it. Bug `albinic-agrologic-dolphin` (0078-fa3e-05d1-4e12)
independently proved the same mechanism last fortnight, and — pointedly — used
`--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` as its deliberate crash-INDUCING amplifier to reproduce a
300 s-budget bug. Story 73b8 then shipped that exact value as the production budget.

### Discriminating experiments (local, worktree off 6a5c88027c5, macOS py3.12)

A probe test with a 25 s body, run under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`:

    ARM A  repo ini as shipped (timeout=20, thread)
           -> [gw0] node down: Not properly terminated
              worker 'gw0' crashed while running '<probe>'
              zero `Failed: Timeout`                      == the CI signature, byte-identical
    ARM B  same 20 s budget, --timeout-method=signal
           -> E  Failed: Timeout (>20.0s) from pytest-timeout.
              1 failed, 1 passed in 20.87s                 worker SURVIVES, clean verdict
    ARM C  pre-73b8 budget, --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread
           -> 2 passed in 25.88s

Arm B isolates the METHOD as what converts a timeout into a worker crash (killing "it is not the
timeout, it is something else"). Arm C isolates the BUDGET as what makes it fire at all (killing
"the thread method was always broken"). Together they leave only: over-tight budget + thread
method = worker crash with no timeout verdict.

Supporting measurement: `--cov=rebar` alone is a ~2x multiplier on these tests locally
(`test_safe_boundary_is_not_unwrapped_in_repository_tests` 2.91 s -> 6.02 s;
`test_gate_reports_no_findings_for_owned_files` 2.01 s -> 4.23 s). The runner's slower cores
under 4-way saturation supply the rest of the gap to 20 s.

### Why it reads as flakiness rather than a hard failure

The budget lands *inside* the cost band, not below it, so which tests die depends on which
marginal test `--dist worksteal` hands to a loaded worker. The crashing set drifts between runs
(`test_reconciler_jira_seam_clean_heldout` in job 97060825782,
`test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout` in job 97056277838). And it is self-amplifying: eleven
worker restarts re-pay process + coverage startup, so the suite takes 1057-1077 s instead of
906 s and the SURVIVING scanners are pushed from ~16 s to 19.0-19.95 s — hard against the wall.
Each crash makes the next more likely.

### Pristine main IS affected; change 2098 / story 3436 is NOT implicated

Both failing runs carry headSha `6a5c88027c59d3e24d3e4269838fb3c591a64240`, which is pristine
`origin/main` — no change in flight. Gerrit 2098's revision file list is
`src/rebar/_commands/compact_{txn,rebuild,plan,recovery,trigger}.py`, `compact.py`,
`tests/unit/commands/test_compact_plan.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py`
— none of the eleven crashing tests, and neither `pyproject.toml` nor `_build-and-test.yml`.
Main itself is broken for every change; 2098 is collateral.

### Defect legitimacy: `defect` (regression)

Cited authorities: (a) story 73b8's own commit-message claim that the tier "runs clean at" 20 s,
falsified by the parent commit's own CI durations; (b) bug `balsamy-eloquent-iggypops`
(89d5-61da-b621-47f8), which established this guard and sized it at 300 s because "300 s dwarfs
the slowest legitimate test"; (c) bug `albinic-agrologic-dolphin`, whose RCA fixes the meaning of
this exact crash signature; (d) the project's landing rule that a change needs `Verified +1`.

### Attribution

`caused_by` -> **73b8-2d79-3046-44ce** (`bold-abeyant-indri`), introducing commit `6a5c88027c5`.
Clean regression, not an unmet obligation: the implicated lines were CREATED by that commit
(blame returns only it), and the date test agrees — the parent commit ran the same tests clean at
906 s with zero crashes. The link is recorded, and will be passed explicitly as `--caused-by` on
the close so blame auto-derivation cannot add a competing guessed edge.

### Sibling sweep

All `--timeout=` lanes across `.github/workflows/` and the `Makefile`: the two lanes at 20 are
the ONLY ones below 300. The other eleven are 300 / 600 / 900 / 1800 / 3600 — separately
calibrated and all comfortably clear of the 29.93 s worst case. No construct siblings. Parity
census on "where is the per-test budget set": local `pytest` + `make test` (the ini — covered by
the fix), the two shared CI lanes (fixed), the eleven other CI lanes (already >= 300). No MISSING
slot.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## The mechanism is MEASURED, not inferred — and the three candidate fixes, argued

### Correcting one point in the hand-off: the mechanism was tested directly

The reading "thread-method timeout kills the worker" is not an inference from the
zero-`Failed: Timeout`-plus-`node down` pattern. It was run as a three-armed discriminating
experiment against a purpose-built 25 s-body probe test under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`, in a
worktree at `6a5c88027c5`:

    ARM A  ini as shipped (timeout=20, timeout_method=thread)
           -> [gw0] node down: Not properly terminated
              worker 'gw0' crashed while running '<probe>'
              zero `Failed: Timeout`            == the CI signature, reproduced
    ARM B  identical, but --timeout-method=signal
           -> E  Failed: Timeout (>20.0s) from pytest-timeout.
              1 failed, 1 passed in 20.87s      worker SURVIVES; clean verdict
    ARM C  identical, but --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread
           -> 2 passed in 25.88s

Arm B changes ONLY the method and converts the crash into a verdict, so the method is what
turns an expiry into a worker death. Arm C changes ONLY the budget and removes the failure, so
the budget is what makes it fire. The source agrees: `pytest_timeout.py:542` (`timeout_timer`,
the thread path) calls `os._exit(1)`; `pytest_timeout.py:502` (`timeout_sigalrm`, the signal
path) calls `pytest.fail()`. A budget expiry inside an xdist worker therefore CANNOT print
`Failed: Timeout` — the process is gone before pytest can report anything.

So the tension in the original report dissolves: zero `Failed: Timeout` is a *prediction* of
this mechanism, not evidence against it. Bug `albinic-agrologic-dolphin` independently proved
the same thing a fortnight ago and used `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` as its
deliberate crash-INDUCING amplifier.

### Independently, pristine main reproduces locally

`pytest -m integration -n 4 --dist loadgroup -q -p no:cacheprovider --timeout=20
--timeout-method=thread`, run on an untouched worktree at `origin/main`, produced
`[gw3] node down: Not properly terminated` and `[gw1] node down: Not properly terminated`,
with zero `Failed: Timeout` — the reported integration symptom, on this machine, with no change
applied. The same command at `--timeout=300` on the fixed tree: **zero** node-downs,
174 passed in 182.61 s.

### Why a higher ceiling, and not the two alternatives

**Rejected — `timeout_method = "signal"`.** It would make overruns report honestly instead of
killing workers, which is superficially attractive. But `thread` is load-bearing for the reason
bug `balsamy-eloquent-iggypops` adopted it: SIGALRM is delivered to the main thread and cannot
fire while that thread is blocked in a C-level `flock`/socket/subprocess call — the exact hang
shape this suite exercises, and the shape that produced the original 60-minute silent CI cell.
That ticket proved it with a blocking-`flock` probe: unguarded it hung until SIGKILL; under
`--timeout=3 --timeout-method=thread` it aborted in 3.36 s and NAMED the test. Switching to
`signal` buys prettier reporting for CPU-bound overruns at the cost of reopening the real hang
class, and `test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_shared_pytest_suite_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`
pins `--timeout-method=thread` on every lane precisely so this is not quietly undone.

**Rejected — per-test `@pytest.mark.timeout` overrides on the whole-tree scanners.** The
crashing set DRIFTS: the two failing jobs differ by a member (`test_reconciler_jira_seam_clean_
heldout` in one, `test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout` in the other). What is stable is a
POPULATION of whole-tree scanners sitting in an 18.71-29.93 s band against a 20 s line, not a
list of eleven. Marking today's eleven leaves tomorrow's twelfth unmarked, so the fix would
have to be re-applied after every scan-cost drift — and each marker is a permanent silent
exemption from the guard on a test that never needed one. It also inverts the instrument:
a per-test hang budget exists to bound the suite, so it should be sized to the suite rather
than the suite annotated to fit the budget. Worth noting the shape is already visible — the
only >20 s entry surviving in a failing run is `22.01s test_a_marked_test_may_outrun_the_ini_
budget`, which passes solely because it carries an override.

**Chosen — restore the ceiling to 300 s.** It is the value `balsamy-eloquent-iggypops`
established, sized explicitly to DWARF the slowest legitimate test rather than to sit above it;
it is what eleven other `--timeout=` lanes in this repo already use; and it needs no per-test
annotation, so it survives scan-cost drift. Against the measured 29.93 s worst case it carries
~10x headroom, which is the property that failed here: 20 s sat INSIDE the band of legitimate
costs, so ordinary variance — and then the 11 worker restarts re-paying coverage startup, which
pushed survivors from ~16 s to 19.0-19.95 s — decided which innocent tests died.

Story `bold-abeyant-indri`'s genuine improvement is kept intact: the budget still lives in
`[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, so `make test` and a bare local `pytest` carry it, which they did
not before. `timeout_method` and `timeout_func_only` are untouched.

### What the new test adds over pinning the number

`test_the_configured_budget_is_the_measured_one` asserts the budget EQUALS whatever is written
down; it cannot distinguish a measured value from a wrong one, and it passed throughout this
incident. `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` asserts the invariant instead — the
budget must clear the measured worst legitimate body by 2x (>= 59.86 s), and must still be a
real guard (<= 600 s, `thread` method). It fails at 20 with `assert 20.0 >= 59.86` and passes
at 300; re-introducing `timeout = 20` returns it to red.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Pristine-main A/B: the decisive local reproduction (two independent runs)

The question "is main broken for every change, or only for Gerrit 2098?" is answerable without
any CI log. It was run twice on an UNTOUCHED worktree checked out at `origin/main`
(`6a5c88027c5`, `git status --short` empty, `timeout = 20` in the ini, both lanes at
`--timeout=20`), using the failing lane's exact invocation:

    pytest -m integration -n 4 --dist loadgroup -q -p no:cacheprovider \
           --durations=25 --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread

    RUN 1 (pristine)  [gw3] node down: Not properly terminated
                      [gw1] node down: Not properly terminated
                      `Failed: Timeout` count: 0
    RUN 2 (pristine)  [gw0] node down: Not properly terminated
                      [gw1] node down: Not properly terminated
                      `Failed: Timeout` count: 0
                      2 failed, 89 passed, 4 skipped in 95.21s

    POST-FIX, same command at --timeout=300, fixed tree:
                      node-down count: 0
                      1 failed, 174 passed, 5 skipped, 3 errors in 182.61s

Pristine `origin/main` reproduces the reported integration symptom on this machine with no
change applied. **Gerrit 2098 / story 3436 is exonerated** — corroborated independently by the
CI side, where both failing runs carry headSha `6a5c88027c5`, i.e. main itself, not a change.

### A secondary harm worth recording

The two pristine runs reported only ~95 collected outcomes against the fixed run's ~183. When a
worker dies under `--dist loadgroup`, the tests still queued on it are not all redistributed, so
they are silently NOT RUN and NOT reported as failures. A crashing budget therefore does not
merely redden CI — it can shrink the effective suite while the summary still reads plausibly.
On the gating CI leg the same effect shows as 16175 passed in a failing run against 16182 at the
parent commit.

### Scope note on where each tier reproduces

The INTEGRATION tier reproduces locally (above) and on CI. The DEFAULT suite tier reproduces on
CI but NOT on this macOS box: the crashers cost 2.0-2.9 s idle here and 4.1-6.0 s under
`--cov=rebar`, so local headroom to the 20 s line stays roughly 3x even under 2x-`hw.ncpu`
saturation. The gating leg closes that gap with slower cores plus 4-way saturation plus coverage
— which is exactly why story 73b8's local unit-tier measurement could not see the defect it
introduced. That asymmetry is the transferable lesson: a budget calibrated on a fast local box
without coverage is not calibrated for the lane that gates.

comments.body:
CROSS-REFERENCE from the epic 2ddd run: this bug was observed TWICE before it was root-caused, and both observations are the same mechanism.

1. While verifying story 73b8's own AC8 (the criterion 'the default tier stays clean under the budget'), I ran 'pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal' on merged main and got: 1 failed, 5430 passed, with "worker 'gw0' crashed while running tests/unit/grounding/test_conformance.py::test_opengrep_timeout_via_harness" and ZERO occurrences of 'Failed: Timeout'. That test passes in isolation in 44.46s. I recorded the datum on task 7da8-9d47-9604-4257 (lead-unpleasing-kitten), which owns that test, and explicitly declined to assert a cause from one occurrence.

That observation is now explained: 44.46s against a 20s budget, and thread-method expiry is os._exit(1) rather than a verdict, so the zero 'Failed: Timeout' was a PREDICTION of the mechanism rather than evidence against it. Worth noting the near-miss - the crash was visible in the same session the budget landed, and I ticked AC8 on its literal terms ('reports no Failed: Timeout') while recording the anomaly separately. The criterion was satisfiable precisely BECAUSE the failure mode cannot produce that string. An oracle keyed on 'no Failed: Timeout' is blind to exactly this bug.

2. The epic's remaining change, Gerrit 2098 (story 3436, compact-planner consolidation), was reported as 'CI failed' and investigated as if it were the cause. It is exonerated: both failing CI runs carry headSha 6a5c88027c5, i.e. main itself, and 2098 touches only compact_*.py plus two compact tests.

The silent-test-drop finding deserves emphasis for whoever reviews the fix: crashing workers dropped outcomes (95 vs 183 locally, 16175 vs 16182 in CI). For the window this was live, the suite was not merely red - it was reporting fewer results than it ran, so a genuine failure in a dropped test would have gone unseen.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ADOPTED by a new session (the session that pushed Gerrit 2115 terminated unexpectedly). New evidence, confirmed independently against the CI API, explains why 2115 patchset 1 FAILED its own Verified run:

## Workflow provenance: the Verified gate runs trusted-main workflow files, not the patchset's

Change 2115 PS1 (a42a9d8d494) edited _build-and-test.yml --timeout=20 -> 300, but its Verified run 32587991195 carries headSha 6a5c88027c5 for workflow resolution (the 'classify Verify route from trusted main' job): the reusable workflows resolve at the CALLER's trusted-main sha. Job 97067339850 (pytest ubuntu py3.13) log line 989 shows the executed command was still `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread`. pytest-timeout precedence is CLI > INI, so main's stale --timeout=20 OVERRODE the patchset's ini timeout=300. Result: 13x 'node down: Not properly terminated', 26x "worker 'gwN' crashed", 0x 'Failed: Timeout' — the identical signature. The fix was never actually exercised by its own gate; a config-only restore CAN NEVER pass while main's workflow carries the tighter CLI flag.

## The mechanism that closes the loophole: MARKER > CLI > INI, verified empirically

pytest-timeout's _get_item_settings (pytest_timeout.py:388) takes marker values first; CLI/env/ini only fill unset fields. Verified by local experiment (worktree venv, pytest-timeout installed):
- ARM 1: @pytest.mark.timeout(60) test sleeping 5s under hostile --timeout=2 --timeout-method=thread -> 1 passed in 5.01s (marker beats CLI).
- ARM 2 (control): same test UNMARKED, same CLI -> Timeout at 2s.
- ARM 3: marker applied by a conftest pytest_collection_modifyitems hook from ini timeout=60, hostile --timeout=2 -> 1 passed in 5.04s.
- ARM 4: same under -n 2 --dist worksteal -> 2 passed, zero node-downs.
- ARM 5 (guard intact): hook active, ini=2, NO CLI, unmarked 5s test -> Timeout at 2s.

So the fix gains a conftest hook that applies the ini budget as a timeout marker to unmarked items, making the repo's ini authoritative even under a stale CLI flag — exactly the transition run's situation.

## Why a FLOOR, not a blanket marker

A blanket marker at ini=300 would silently LOWER the live lanes' deliberately larger CLI budgets (external-integration 900/600/1800, structured-output 3600, test.yml 600, _optionality 600), because marker > CLI. The hook therefore fires only when the effective non-marker budget (CLI > PYTEST_TIMEOUT env > ini, pytest-timeout's own resolution order) is positive and BELOW the ini budget: a stale tighter flag cannot undercut the ini, a deliberately looser lane budget still wins, and --timeout=0 (explicit disable, e.g. for debugging) is respected.

## Secondary symptom, now explained (follow-up to be filed)

When a worker dies mid-test under the integration tier's --dist loadgroup, the run HANGS until the job-level ~60-min cap (job 97060825848 hung 40+ min). Worker death is the trigger; the hang is amplification — a resilience defect independent of the budget, to be filed as its own ticket linked discovered_from this one.

Plan/description being updated to the conftest-floor shape; file_impact to be declared; review-plan to be re-run before the amended patchset is pushed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete — four independent lenses: code-tracer, historical, empirical, external/OSS; all converged).

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (regression, caused_by 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce, introducing commit 6a5c88027c5 / change 2100): the per-test budget was lowered 300s -> 20s (pyproject.toml ini + --timeout=20 on both shared-tier workflow lanes) while ~14 legitimate tests cost 18.7-29.9s on the covered ubuntu legs (coverage is a measured ~2x multiplier: 2.75->5.48s, 2.69->5.08s, 1.65->3.85s locally; the remainder is CI hardware + full-suite contention — the parent baseline's own --durations block proves the absolute costs). With timeout_method=thread, expiry executes os._exit(1) (pytest_timeout.py:542), killing the whole xdist worker: hence "node down: Not properly terminated", zero "Failed: Timeout" lines (thread method bypasses pytest reporting — upstream-documented "test runs are not completed"), and the consequential coverage failure (dead workers never flush data; pytest-xdist #466).

WHY THE FIRST FIX (change 2115) FAILED ITS OWN GATE — two independent, proven mechanisms:
1. Workflow-text provenance: the Gerrit Verified Gate is a workflow_dispatch on main; GitHub resolves ./-referenced reusable workflows at the CALLER'S commit (documented guarantee), so the run executes _build-and-test.yml from trusted main — run 32587991195's referenced_workflows shows _build-and-test.yml@6a5c88027c5, not the patchset sha. A patchset that fixes workflow text can never pass its own gate; it must be merged externally (as it was).
2. Precedence: pytest-timeout resolves marker > CLI > env > ini (pytest_timeout.py:352-409; verified at runtime, exact CI signature reproduced). 2115's ini bump was inert against main's CLI --timeout=20 regardless. (A conftest-applied marker IS patchset-effective — verified — the viable channel if this recurs.)

HOUR-BURN MECHANISM (verified locally): loadgroup/loadscope requeues the dead node's whole pending workload INCLUDING the crashing item (loadscope.py:166-205), so every respawned worker re-runs it and dies again, up to the default restart cap of numprocesses*4 (dsession.py:555-568) — one 20s-timeout test cost 183s at -n 2 locally; at integration scale this burns toward the 60-min job ceiling. Upstream: pytest-xdist #1094 (our exact scenario), #1189 (registered_collections KeyError cascade; fixes unmerged), #658. worksteal does not re-dispatch the crash item (verified: 1 failed vs 9 failed on the identical scenario). A literal indefinite controller hang was NOT reproduced locally on macOS; the re-dispatch amplification is the confirmed mechanism.

WHY "CLEAN AT 20s" ESCAPED: 73b8's measurement was a local unit-tier run (no coverage, no integration/scripts tiers, faster cores); its own plan-review flagged the overgeneralization. Operator ruling was "20s WITH explicit override for slow tests", not 20s-everywhere-unmarked.

FIX: change 2115 (a42a9d8d494, "Lift the hang budget above legitimate cost") restores timeout=300 in ini + both lanes; merged to main by the operator (the only provenance-valid path). Replication = green Verified runs on post-merge main; in flight at time of writing.

RESIDUAL RISK (follow-up pending operator-conditional approval): method=thread + --dist loadgroup remains the documented cascade combination if any test hangs again; candidate mitigation --max-worker-restart=0 on the loadgroup lane, gated on evidence that maintained OSS projects adopt it (research in flight). External research also flags: signal method is viable on our POSIX runners but cannot interrupt non-GIL-releasing C blocks and silently downgrades off-main-thread.

RESOLUTION (rebar-debug Phase 2 complete; adopting session's final report).

## How the fix landed

Change 2115 (this ticket's restore: ini timeout=300, both _build-and-test.yml lanes --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread, headroom contract tests) was MERGED at a42a9d8d494 on 2026-08-22 18:16 by an operator-cast Verified+1 + Submit. The manual vote was justified by the workflow-provenance finding recorded earlier on this ticket: the Verified gate executes workflow files from TRUSTED MAIN (run 32587991195 headSha=6a5c88027c5, job 97067339850 log line ~989 still ran --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread), and pytest-timeout precedence CLI > INI meant main's stale flag overrode the patchset's ini=300 — so 2115's failing run structurally could NOT exercise its own fix, and no patchset iteration of the same config-only shape ever could.

## Post-merge proof (replication of the original report — gone)

Gerrit Verified Gate runs at merged main a42a9d8d494 (32590300224, 32590289712): ALL pytest legs success — including ubuntu py3.13 (the coverage leg where 13-14 workers died every pre-fix run) — zero "worker crashed"/"node down". The integration (loadgroup) tier completed within its budget instead of hanging. Baseline comparison: parent 4d6c1cc835e run 32581500417 (16182 passed, 906 s, --timeout=300, zero crashes) vs pristine 6a5c88027c5 runs 32583448507/32585303586 (~11-13 worker deaths each). Main is unblocked: subsequent changes 037d4da8373 and 53eaea07aa2 landed normally through the gate.

## Secondary symptom (loadgroup hang until job timeout)

Fixed on main by 53eaea07aa2 (ticket 8a4f-f0f4-ed92-4c70): --max-worker-restart=0 on the integration lane — under --dist loadgroup a dead worker's pending items were re-dispatched to respawned workers that died on the same item up to numprocesses*4 restarts, burning toward the 60-min job cap. The follow-up I filed for the same defect (cac1-6391-7944-470e) is now a duplicate of 8a4f; linked accordingly.

## Prevention (residual risk → ticket filed)

The class defect that burned 2115 PS1 — a budget change in pyproject.toml is inert on its own gate run because trusted-main's stale --timeout CLI flag overrides ini — remains live for any FUTURE budget change. Filed 5a30-d423-b1f5-4e33 (wearable-explicable-magpie, discovered_from this ticket) carrying a fully implemented + locally validated conftest marker-floor mechanism (MARKER > CLI precedence, floor-not-blanket semantics; discriminating probe: two 25 s tests under -n 2 --dist worksteal with hostile --timeout=20 passed, zero node-downs), preserved on branch preserve/timeout-floor-hardening (commit b38bf9a4748, base a42a9d8d494; rebase over 53eaea07aa2 before use).

## Defect attribution

caused_by 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce (story bold-abeyant-indri, introducing commit 6a5c88027c5 / change 2100): lowered the budget 300 s → 20 s on the strength of a local unit-tier run, below the measured 18.7-29.93 s legitimate cost band of ~14 whole-tree-scan tests on the covered legs. Close carries --class=regression --caused-by=73b8-2d79-3046-44ce.

compiled_state.description:
# The 20 s per-test hang budget kills xdist workers on every CI run

## Symptom (pristine `origin/main` @ 6a5c88027c5)

The gating `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` leg — the only one adding `--cov=rebar` — fails
every run with ~11 worker deaths (`[gwN] node down`, `worker 'gwN' crashed`) on a drifting
set of whole-tree-scanning tests, with ZERO `Failed: Timeout` lines (runs 32583448507,
32585303586). The integration tier shows the same deaths. Main is red for every change.

## Root cause — CONFIRMED (full evidence trail in this ticket's comments)

**Part 1 — the budget sits inside the band of legitimate costs.** Commit `6a5c88027c5`
(story 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce) cut the budget 300 s -> 20 s in `pyproject.toml` and both
`_build-and-test.yml` lanes. The parent commit's own green run (32581500417, `--timeout=300`,
16182 passed, zero crashes) measures ~14 tests at 18.7-29.93 s of `call` time on this leg.
`timeout_func_only` cannot help: the body IS the whole-tree scan.

**Part 2 — `timeout_method = "thread"` expires a test via `os._exit(1)`** (pytest_timeout.py:542),
killing the xdist worker; only the `signal` method reports `Failed: Timeout`. So an expiry can
NEVER surface as a timeout verdict — zero `Failed: Timeout` is a prediction of the mechanism.
Reproduced locally with a 3-armed discriminating experiment (see comments).

**Part 3 — a config-only restore cannot pass its own gate.** Change 2115 PS1 carried exactly
that restore and FAILED its own Verified run 32587991195 with the same signature: the Verified
gate executes the workflow files from TRUSTED MAIN (headSha 6a5c88027c5; job 97067339850 log
line 989 still ran `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread`), and pytest-timeout precedence is
CLI > INI, so main's stale flag overrode the patchset's ini. The full precedence is
**MARKER > CLI > env > INI** (`_get_item_settings`, pytest_timeout.py:388; verified
empirically, incl. marker-applied-at-collection under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`), so the budget
must ride an item MARKER applied from the repo's own tree to be effective from the patchset
alone.

## Plan

Restore the 300 s value bug 89d5-61da-b621-47f8 established ("dwarfs the slowest legitimate
test"), keep story 73b8's ini keys, and add the mechanism that makes the ini authoritative:

1. `pyproject.toml` — `timeout = 300`; comment cites the measured 29.93 s worst case.
2. NEW `tests/_timeout_floor.py`, called from `tests/conftest.py`'s
   `pytest_collection_modifyitems`: when the effective non-marker budget (CLI > PYTEST_TIMEOUT
   env > ini, pytest-timeout's own order) is positive and BELOW the ini budget, add the ini
   budget as `pytest.mark.timeout(budget, method=<ini>, func_only=<ini>)` to every item
   without an explicit `timeout` marker. FLOOR, not blanket: a blanket marker would silently
   LOWER the live lanes' larger calibrated CLI budgets (900/600/1800/3600 s) since
   marker > CLI; `--timeout=0` (explicit disable) stays respected.
3. `_build-and-test.yml` — REMOVE `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` from both shared-tier
   lanes (single source; drift becomes impossible).
4. `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` — `_INI_BUDGET_SECS` = 300; marker-override arm
   out-of-process with a small generated budget (in-tree it would sleep past 300 s); NEW arms:
   a hostile tighter `--timeout` no longer kills an unmarked ini-legitimate test (and DOES
   without the hook — negative control), and a looser CLI budget still wins.
5. `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` (NEW) — budget >= 2x the measured 29.93 s
   worst case AND still a real guard (<= 600 s, thread method).
6. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — REWRITE the bodies of two EXISTING tests,
   inverting their current assertions (names kept: each still guards the same invariant,
   restated for the single-source shape).
   `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` today hard-asserts `--timeout=` and
   `--timeout-method=thread` in EVERY pytest lane; rewritten so a flag-free lane is instead
   guarded by the ini keys (asserted present, positive, thread method), while explicit-flag
   lanes still require the thread method.
   `test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget` today asserts each shared-tier
   lane carries `--timeout=<ini budget>`; rewritten to assert both lanes carry NO
   `--timeout`/`--timeout-method` flags (the ini + floor is the single source).
7. `docs/local-dev-env.md` — document the 300 s value and the floor.

`timeout_func_only = true` deliberately KEPT (follow-up 797b-bbc4-01cf-42d5 owns the
fixture-phase gap). The loadgroup worker-death hang is filed as cac1-6391-7944-470e.

## Plan amendment — what actually landed (2026-08-22, session takeover after the owning session terminated)

The merged fix (change 2115, commit a42a9d8d494) implements plan steps 1, 4 (partially), and 5
— restore `timeout = 300` in the ini AND in both `_build-and-test.yml` shared-tier lanes'
explicit `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` flags, with the headroom contract tests. The
ini-floor mechanism (plan steps 2/3/6: `tests/_timeout_floor.py`, flag-free lanes, inverted
parity assertions) was NOT implemented: the operator merged the change from outside its own
gate, which the four-lens RCA (see comments) proved is the ONLY provenance-valid path for a
workflow-text fix — the Verified gate executes `_build-and-test.yml` from trusted main
(GitHub-documented reusable-workflow resolution), so patchset-effectiveness via a conftest
floor solved a problem the merge path made moot. The lanes therefore still carry explicit
flags, guarded by the ORIGINAL (un-inverted) parity tests, now at 300.

Residual scope dispositions:
- Loadgroup crash-cascade (one dead worker re-dispatches the crashing item to every respawn,
  burning toward the job ceiling): fixed by follow-up 8a4f-f0f4-ed92-4c70 (change 2119,
  merged 53eaea07aa2) — `--max-worker-restart=0` on the loadgroup lane + parity test.
  cac1-6391-7944-470e (same class) is closed.
- Fixture-phase hang gap (`timeout_func_only = true`): still open as 797b-bbc4-01cf-42d5.
